question.text: Force between two point charges <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>q</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> placed in vacuum at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math> apart is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>F</mi></math>. Force between them when placed in a medium having dielectric <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>5</mn></math> at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>r</mi><mn>5</mn></mfrac></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>cm</mi></math> apart will be:

solution.text:
Using Coulomb's law, we can write:

In air F=14πε0q1q2r2

In medium F'=14πKε0q1q2r'2=14π5ε025q1q2r2=5F
